title: Kid Rena and the Creole Serenaders' distinctive styles
summary: Penn says Kid Rena and Dwight Newman's Creole Serenaders played in unmistakably different ways from other bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you just a few more, one or two more things. We spoke about Buddy Petit and his style, Chris Kelly and his style. What about Kid René? We didn't say too much about his style.
Well, what I know about René, René, he had a different style of playing music. You know they had another band used to play in the city here. Newman's band.
Yeah. What was his name? Creole Serenators.
Creole Serenators, yeah. Dwight Newman was the leader?

Now the Creole Serenators and René, those two bands, were the only two bands that would play different from the rest of the bands. Now René had a way of playing that nobody else used to play like. You could tell René that he was in the hall playing. You didn't have to go look in there, you'd know it was René, because he had a different way of playing. Just like the Creole Serenators. And that's another band that had a different way of playing.
What do you mean by a different way of playing?

Well they just played different from the way we play or any other band. They have a different way of playing. And you can tell it. Was it more jazzy or less jazzy? Well some people said it wasn't, and some people said it wasn't, but most of them said it wasn't, you see.
Did they have about the same kind of a line-up of the band though, same kind of pieces?

Well they had the same kind of line-up that we or any other band have. It's just the way they used to play was a little different, the way they had their band range and play their music was different. And René, the way he played trumpet, nobody else used to play no trumpet like him because it was just a different style he was playing in, but he could play.
Nobody had ever played much like him before you don't think?
No, not that I know. Not that I know. He's one man was a different trumpet player. And it was nice the way the people said it was.
